ai.description: *Raorchestes marki* is a small bush frog (SVL 20–22 mm). It has a brown dorsum with dark markings, a distinct white spot on the snout, and a granular belly. It lacks webbing on the fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes marki* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes marki inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes marki* is a nocturnal frog that remains hidden within dense vegetation during the day, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes marki* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes marki* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-altitude shola forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes marki* consists of a series of short, high-pitched metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in mid-elevation forests.
